title: Verbal Adverbs 6: Style and the когда Choice
description: Verbal adverbs are a written-register feature. Today: when to choose a gerund and when a когда clause is more natural, and how to chain several gerunds under one subject. Negation gets its own lesson next.
descriptionRussian: Деепричастие - это конструкция письменной речи. Сегодня: когда выбрать деепричастие, а когда естественнее конструкция с «когда», и как соединять несколько деепричастий при одном подлежащем. Отрицание - в следующем уроке.
intro: An honest lesson about register. These forms are a written-language feature, and in ordinary speech Russians usually prefer a full clause even where a verbal adverb would be correct. That is worth knowing before you start putting them into conversation, where they can sound like someone reading aloud from a report.
rules: Verbal adverbs are a written-register feature. In casual speech, native speakers usually prefer когда + a finite verb even when both forms are grammatical.
Negation puts не directly before the gerund. Не зная, не понимая, не глядя are everyday B2 phrases.
Several gerunds can chain in one sentence as long as they all share the subject of the main verb. Aspects can mix within the chain if the timing fits.
Gerund clauses are always set off by commas. Sentence-initial position is the default; sentence-final works but feels more literary.
examples: Не зная ответа, она молчала. (Not knowing the answer, she stayed silent.)
Не понимая инструкций, Иван попросил помощи. (Not understanding the instructions, Ivan asked for help.)
Не глядя на часы, Антон работал до утра. (Without looking at the clock, Anton worked until morning.)
Войдя в комнату, увидев гостей и улыбнувшись, Маша сняла пальто. (A chain of three perfective gerunds; all three share the subject Маша.)
Открыв дверь, я вошёл. (Written register: a compact gerund.)
Когда я открыл дверь, я вошёл. (Spoken register: the когда clause feels more natural in conversation.)

items.prompt: Recap from L5: which sentence breaks the same-subject rule?
items.hint: Find the option whose two verbs have different subjects.
items.explanation: Recap from L5: in 'Открывая окно, упала ваза,' I open the window but the vase falls; different subjects. The other three sentences each have a single shared subject.

items.prompt: In which register is a gerund construction MOST natural?
items.promptEnglish: When are gerunds at home stylistically?
items.hint: Recall the register of the gerund construction in modern Russian.
items.explanation: Verbal adverbs belong to the written register. Native speakers reach for them in essays, articles, and literature; in conversation, they prefer когда + finite verbs even when the gerund is grammatical. A spoken sentence full of gerunds reads as bookish.

items.prompt: How is negation marked on a verbal adverb?
items.promptEnglish: Where does the не particle go?
options: Inside the gerund as a prefix: незная
Directly before the gerund: не зная
Negation is impossible with gerunds; rewrite with когда
items.answer: Directly before the gerund: не зная
items.hint: Negation works the same way as on any verb form.
items.explanation: The particle не sits directly before the gerund, just as it does with finite verbs and infinitives: не зная, не понимая, не глядя. These are everyday phrases. The other options describe non-existent patterns; gerund negation is fully regular.

items.promptEnglish: Not knowing the answer, Masha stayed silent.
items.hint: Negation goes directly before the gerund as a separate word.
items.explanation: Не зная is the standard negated imperfective gerund of знать. The particle stays separate from the gerund (a single space, no fusion). 'Знав не' has the wrong word order; 'незная' tries to fuse the particle into the form, which Russian does not do; 'без' takes the genitive case and is a different construction (без знания, 'without knowledge').

items.prompt: Pick the sentence that flows naturally as a written-register narrative.
items.promptEnglish: Which option uses the gerund in its natural register?
options: Когда я открыл дверь и когда я увидел гостей, я улыбнулся.
Открыв дверь и увидев гостей, я улыбнулся.
Я открыл дверь. Я увидел гостей. Я улыбнулся.
Открыв дверь, увидя гостей, и я улыбнулся.
items.answer: Открыв дверь и увидев гостей, я улыбнулся.
items.hint: Written register prefers compact gerund chains over repeated когда clauses.
items.explanation: The chained gerunds Открыв and увидев compress two prior actions into a smooth narrative line that reads as natural written Russian. The first option is grammatical but sounds heavy with repeated когда; the third is grammatical but choppy and would suit a children's book; the fourth has a malformed gerund (увидя is non-standard) and a stray и.

items.promptEnglish: Not understanding the instructions, Anton asked for help.
items.hint: The slot needs a negated imperfective gerund (state of not understanding holds during the asking).
items.explanation: Не понимая is the negated imperfective gerund of понимать. The not-understanding is a state simultaneous with the asking. Не понимать is the negated infinitive; не понимал is the negated finite past; не понять is the negated perfective infinitive.

blanks: _____ на часы, Антон работал до утра.
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Negated imperfective gerund (a fixed-feel B2 phrase).
hints: The not-looking holds during the working. Which form is the negated imperfective gerund of глядеть?
explanations: Не глядя на часы is a near-fixed phrase in Russian, equivalent to 'without looking at the clock.' Не глядеть is the negated infinitive; не глядел is the negated finite past; без + infinitive is not a Russian construction (без takes a noun in the genitive).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was opening the door, the vase fell.
errorCorrection.explanation: The same-subject rule says the gerund and the main verb must share a doer, but the subject of упала is ваза (the vase), and the vase is not opening the door, so Открывая dangles. Russian repairs this with a когда clause that has its own subject: Когда я открывал дверь. Открыв дверь is a perfective gerund that still dangles and only changes the timing to a completed prior action, and Открывая двери just pluralizes the object ('doors') without fixing the missing subject. English allows the loose attachment, but Russian does not.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Not hearing the question, Anton asked again.
errorCorrection.explanation: Russian negates a gerund by placing the particle не directly before it as a separate word: не слыша. Неслыша fuses the particle into the form, which Russian orthography does not allow for verb forms (unlike adjectives). Без слыша is impossible: без takes nouns.

errorCorrection.sentence: Когда я открыл дверь, и когда я увидел гостей, я улыбнулся.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having opened the door and seen the guests, I smiled.
errorCorrection.error: Когда я открыл дверь, и когда я увидел гостей
errorCorrection.explanation: When one subject performs every action, written Russian compresses the two prior events into a chain of perfective gerunds: Открыв дверь и увидев гостей. The repeated когда + когда version is grammatical but heavy and reads as spoken register. Открывая дверь и увидя гостей is wrong twice over (Открывая is imperfective; увидя is non-standard), and Открыв дверь, и увидев гостей keeps a stray comma plus и that breaks the clean two-gerund chain.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was approaching the house, the rain started.
errorCorrection.explanation: This is the classic dangling gerund: the subject of начался is дождь, and the rain is not approaching the house, so Подходя has no legal subject to attach to. The repair is a когда clause that supplies its own human subject and preserves the timing: Когда я подходил к дому. Подойдя is the perfective gerund and still dangles, merely changing the meaning to a completed prior approach, while Подходив is not a valid form at all. Russian cannot leave the gerund hanging the way English can.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Without thinking about the consequences, Lena agreed.
errorCorrection.explanation: Negation on a gerund is written as the separate particle не before the form: не думая. Недумая fuses не into the gerund, which Russian does not do with verb forms. Не думав substitutes a past-flavoured form where the simultaneous не думая is needed.

errorCorrection.sentence: Когда я закончил работу, я пошёл домой.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having finished the work, I went home.
errorCorrection.explanation: In written narrative register, when one subject performs both actions in sequence, Russian prefers the compact perfective gerund: Закончив работу ('having finished the work'). The когда clause Когда я закончил работу is fully grammatical but belongs to the conversational register, which the written 'having finished' gloss is steering away from. Заканчивая работу is the imperfective gerund ('while finishing'), which makes the actions simultaneous and changes the meaning, and Закончивши работу is the dated -вши variant. The clean written choice is Закончив работу.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was leaving the house, it started to snow.
errorCorrection.explanation: The subject of пошёл (in пошёл снег, 'snow started') is снег, and the snow is not leaving the house, so the gerund Выходя dangles with no legal subject. Russian fixes this with a когда clause that has its own subject: Когда я выходил из дома. Выйдя is the perfective gerund and still dangles, only shifting the meaning to a completed prior exit, while Выходив is not a valid form. The two-subject conflict can only be resolved by dropping the gerund for a когда clause.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Not knowing the answer, she stayed silent.
minimalPairs.explanation: Russian negates the gerund with the particle не placed directly before it. 'Без' takes a noun in the genitive and would need a different construction (без знания), not a gerund.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Having opened the door and seen the guests, I smiled.
minimalPairs.explanation: Both actions are prior completed events sharing my subject; both should be perfective gerunds. Открыв and увидев are the standard perfective forms. 'Открывая' is the imperfective gerund (would mean 'while opening'), and увидя is non-standard.

reviewVocab.definition: style (the register of the speech: written/formal vs spoken/conversational; verbal adverbs are at home in the written register)
negation (the particle не placed directly before a verb form, including gerunds)
reviewVocab.example: Не зная, не понимая, не глядя — это отрицание деепричастия.

reviewVocab.definition: written (the register where verbal adverbs are most natural; literature, journalism, essays)
conversational (the register where Russians prefer когда + finite verb even when the gerund is grammatical)
reviewVocab.example: В разговорной речи 'Когда я открыл дверь' звучит естественнее, чем 'Открыв дверь'.
